what: *** HIS MARRIAGE NAMES THE BRIDE, AND THIS ARCHIVE NEVER HAD HER ***
the record says: Gilberto Lerena, groom, born *** 1878 "Rep. Oriental" ***, parents Gilberto Lerena and Julia Salvanach. Married *** 19 May 1906, Nuestra Senora del Pilar, Recoleta ***. Spouse: *** CIPRIANA SAENS PENA *** (indexed also "Cepriana Saenz Pena").
collection: Argentina, Capital Federal, Catholic Church Records, 1640-1978
what it gives this archive: *** A NEW PERSON, and a surname worth noticing. *** The register carried this marriage with no bride at all. SAENZ PENA is a name that runs through Argentine public life in exactly these years - *** no relationship to either president is asserted or looked for ***, and the surname is not rare enough to carry one.

what: *** AND THEY HAD A SON NAMED GILBERTO ***
the record says: Gilberto Lerena, *** father ***, spouse "Cepriana Saenz Pena", child *** "Gilberto de Jesus del Corazon" *** (the index bleeds "Aires" into the surname field from the place).
collection: Argentina, Capital Federal, Catholic Church Records, 1640-1978
what it gives this archive: *** THIS IS THE SON THE 1928 IDENTIFICATION PREDICTED. *** The CEMLA arrival has Gilberto b.1879 travelling with a son Gilberto, *** estudiante ***, aged twelve. Yesterday that son was a curiosity. Today he is in a parish index, from a marriage of 1906.

what: *** BUT HIS BIRTH YEAR IS NOT INDEXED, SO THE TEST STILL FAILS ***
the record says: A second search - LERENA, GILBERTO, Argentina, *** births 1910-1920 *** - returns 10 records and *** none of them is this child ***. The birth filter demonstrably works: it cut 63 to 10.
what it gives this archive: *** SO 1916 IS UNCONFIRMED AND THE PAIR STAYS UNMERGED. *** The son exists; his age does not. An identification that rests on a name and a year still rests on a name and a year.

what: *** HIS ARGENTINE NATIONALITY IS NOW ON A RECORD, NOT AN INFERENCE ***
the record says: Military service *** March 1922, Distrito Militar 2, Argentina ***; birth *** 1878, Montevideo, Uruguay ***; parents Lerena and Julia Salvanach. A second entry gives *** Montecarlo, Misiones ***.
what it gives this archive: *** A MONTEVIDEO-BORN MAN CARRIED ON AN ARGENTINE MILITARY DISTRICT ROLL. *** That is what the CEMLA passenger's "ARGENTINE" requires, and the register's "Uruguayan/Argentine" is now documented rather than assumed.

what: *** AND THE 1895 INDEX EXPLAINS THE TABLE THAT WAS WRONG ***
the record says: Searching the 1895 census returns the household of Seccion 21, Subdivision 15 as *** Gilberto 1854, Maria E. C. 1869, Maria Luisa 1880, Carlos A. 1884, Raul A. 1886, Maria E. 1890 *** - and *** NOT the seventeen-year-old ***, who is indexed under *** SALVANACH ***, not Lerena.
what it gives this archive: *** THIS IS WHY /argentina/ CARRIED A TABLE OF NINE FOR SIX DAYS. *** It was built from this index, and the index files the eldest son under his mother's surname. The schedule has sixteen lines. Corrected 20 September; recorded here because the next person to build a table from an index deserves the warning.

what: *** NO NEW CHILDREN. THE REGISTER ALREADY HAD THEM ALL ***
the record says: The search returns Gilberto (1854) as father of *** Maria Carlota, Horacio Alfredo, Luis Felipe, Cesar Alberto, Raul and Carlos ***.
what it gives this archive: *** ALL SIX ARE ALREADY IN THE REGISTER *** under LERENA Salvanach. Checked name by name before writing, because this archive added a duplicate of Dominga Llerena on the day it built a gate against duplicates.
